evidence: Read cold, the draft is the second item in his list under 'What I will not use NLP for' ('Here is a list of things I do not do with NLP, to myself or to others'). It is a parallel 'I do not...' item, sits naturally after 'I do not deny people's legitimate signals' (fear is one of those signals), and is a little longer than its neighbours only because it carries its condition. Pronouns: in 'what it's protecting' the only singular noun before 'it' is 'their fear' ('people' is plural), and 'their' is the people, so every pronoun points where it should. Parse: 'before asking what it's protecting' reads the same whether I ask them or they ask, and either way it says the instruction to override fear is not given until what the fear protects has been asked, which is the order condition in his line ('To override fear before asking what the fear protects'). That is exactly what the_change says: the sentence it replaces ('I do not tell people to override their fear') had lost the condition and read as a flat ban, and the draft puts the condition back in the article's own words. Meaning and added claims: 'tell people to override their fear' is not in his fragment, but it is the existing wording of the sentence being replaced, so this change does not introduce it; nothing else is added, no new fact or first-person claim (C03, C04 absent). One nit that does not change the reading and that I did not fail on: the apostrophe in the draft's contraction is a curly one (U+2019) while the section's other apostrophes (people's, isn't) are straight, so a straight apostrophe would match the section. Tell rows: I went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the literal draft in its context and found none PRESENT. Closest calls: T01, because the first person is the frame of his own list, not an inserted stake; T02, because the section is a run of 'I do not' verdicts, but that is his list form and discrete commitments, and the draft only restores a condition inside one item (the repeated 'I do not' is the list's parallel form, so T26 is not unearned repetition); T10, because 'X before Y' is here the sequencing rule itself, not therapeutic 'you don't have to X before Y' packaging; T17, because it is a commitment in a list of his, not a finished aphorism. Linter: 'D9 follows the source order' is a trivial 1/1 agreement for a one-sentence restoration of his own line, and I checked T13 and T09 as it asks and neither is present, so I accept it.
